title: Terraform module: idempotent priv-VPC EKS control-plane bootstrapper with health gating and operator hooks
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a reusable Terraform module that bootstraps the Redwood Private control-plane inside customer VPCs (EKS master/control-plane components and surrounding infra). The module must be idempotent, support safe rolling upgrades, expose health gates for automation pipelines, and include an optional operator-style post-provision hook for lighter-weight drift remediation and emergency repairs.

Goals:
- Provide a single Terraform module that teams can use for new clusters and for controlled upgrades of the control plane.
- Guarantee idempotence across retries and partial failures (clear plan for resource tagging and stable naming).
- Emit healthcheck endpoints and CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics for preflight and post-upgrade gating.
- Integrate canary/blue-green semantics for control-plane Kubernetes upgrades via a lifecycle hook and an operator-managed reconciler.
- Produce comprehensive runtime logs and terraform outputs for the Console to consume (upgrade status, last healthy timestamp, remediation actions).

Constraints & Non-Goals:
- This ticket focuses on the control-plane bootstrap and health gating semantics; nodegroup lifecycle and autoscaling strategy are out-of-scope and will be separate.
- We will not ship a full operator in this change; instead provide a lightweight operator hook and documented interfaces for later operator rollout.

Design highlights / decisions so far:
- Idempotence: use deterministically derived resource names (cluster UUID + logical name), consistent tags, and preflight checks before apply.
- Health gating: expose a cluster-health SNS/HTTP endpoint and CloudWatch metric namespace (redwood.private.cluster/health) with standardized states: PROVISIONING, HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNHEALTHY.
- Upgrades: include a pre-upgrade "canary plan" step that runs terraform plan against a canary substack (isolated control-plane namespace) when enabled; otherwise use staged rollouts with configurable max_unavailable.
- Operator hook: a configurable Lambda endpoint or Helm hook that can be wired to our internal reconciler. The module will output hook URLs and IAM roles.
- Rollback: annotate each apply with run_id and maintain last-known-good snapshot (s3://redwood-private-cluster-state/<cluster>/snapshots) for automated rollbacks.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Merged):
- Module passes idempotence test suite (apply -> taint -> apply -> no divergent resources) in CI.
- Post-provision healthcheck emits HEALTHY within 15 minutes for standard test workloads.
- Upgrade path: documented runbook and a testable canary upgrade that does not degrade traffic in >1 of 5 canary runs.
- Outputs include stable identifiers, hook endpoints, and a 'health_status' terraform output.
- Security review completed for generated IAM roles and KMS usage.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module under modules/private-controlplane (with examples and tests).
- CI pipelines (terragrunt/terra-test) to validate idempotence and upgrade scenarios.
- Confluence spec with runbook and API for health endpoints.
- Example PR integrating module with dedicated provisioning pipeline used by Solutions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: partial applies could leave control-plane in inconsistent state. Mitigation: preflight checks + guarded apply mode (fail early if preflight fails) + snapshot before upgrade.
- Risk: exposing a new endpoint surface area. Mitigation: default to internal-only endpoints (VPC endpoint or signed Lambda) and require opt-in for public webhooks.
